news.t: The Federal Reserve Board released the results of its 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances, its triennial picture of household assets, debt and banking.

The Federal Reserve Board announced an enforcement action against American Express Company addressing, among other things, failures to sufficiently detect and report certain suspicious activity related to money laundering.
The FOMC released the minutes of its Sep 15–16 meeting.
The Federal Reserve Board approved Isabella Bank Corporation, of Mount Pleasant, Michigan, to acquire Grand River Commerce, Inc. and Grand River Bank, of Grandville, Michigan.

reg.t: Regulation O modernization (insider lending): comment period on the proposal extended to Nov 4. Proposed.
Two rules on stress test transparency and stress capital buffer volatility finalized; a separate proposal on modeling fee income is out for comment. Final.
Two GENIUS Act proposals for Board-supervised payment stablecoin issuers (reserve assets, capital, risk management); comment closes 60 days after Federal Register publication. Proposed.

commentary.note: The Generic edition's own text for this close, carried on the tape.
read: The Federal Reserve raised the federal funds target range by a quarter point to 3.75–4.00% on Sep 16, a 12–0 vote, and the September projections put the median federal funds rate at 4.1% for the end of 2026 (central tendency 4.1–4.4%). August headline CPI ran 3.4% and core CPI 2.4%; August headline PCE ran 3.4% and core PCE 3.0%; September nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000 and the September unemployment rate was 4.2%. September CPI is due Wednesday, Oct 14, the week's main data point.

Treasury's Oct 9 close put the 2-year at 4.80%, the 10-year at 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.60%, leaving 2s10s at +44 bp, 3 bp flatter than the day before. On the week, the 10-year is down 4 bp and the 2-year down 3 bp, while the 3-month bill is up 6 bp at 4.25%. Overnight money sits inside the range: EFFR printed 3.88% on Oct 8, with IORB at 3.90%.

For a deposit-funded balance sheet the week's move is small but two-sided. Slightly lower intermediate yields lift AFS market values at the margin and trim new-money yields by the same few basis points; both show up in the next AOCI and EVE run. On the funding side, the top 12-month CD APY on Bankrate's list is 4.75%, above the effective funds rate of 3.88%, so renewal betas on maturing CDs are being tested against a retail bid above overnight wholesale money.

panels.p: SOFR printed 3.87% on Oct 8, inside the 3.75–4.00% target range and below IORB at 3.90%; the 30-day SOFR average was 3.82% on Oct 9. The 2-year at 4.80% sits 92 bp above the 3.88% effective rate. That spread is arithmetic on the published curve, not a reading of futures. The curve rises from the 3-month bill to the 20-year, with 3M10Y at +99 bp and 5s30s at +58 bp, and the 30-year sits 5 bp below the 20-year.

On Bankrate's best-rate lists the top 12-month CD APY is 4.75% and the top high-yield savings APY is 4.27%. These are advertised consumer yields, not comparable one-for-one with a wholesale rate or a cost of funds. The Fed's primary credit rate is 4.00%. Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed mortgage rate averaged 7.40% in the Oct 8 survey, with the 15-year at 6.73%.
